title: Founding HCL from a Delhi barsati
statement: Nadar and colleagues left DCM Data Products to start Hindustan Computers Limited with Rs 187,000, among the earliest Indian IT ventures, initially making calculators and microcomputers.
outcome: HCL survived and outgrew nearly every contemporary; today it is a $13 billion revenue global technology company spanning services and enterprise products.

title: Selling the hardware business to focus on services
statement: Facing the post-liberalization collapse of hardware tariffs and margins, Nadar progressively shifted HCL toward software services and R&D outsourcing, even ceding joint-venture control to partner HP.
outcome: The pivot from products to services anticipated the industry's direction by several years; HCL's engineering-services model became its differentiated engine.

title: Shiv Nadar Foundation — the SSN engineering institution
statement: Nadar founded the SSN College of Engineering in Chennai and progressively endowed it, later building Shiv Nadar University and VidyaGyan schools for rural gifted students.
outcome: The foundation has funded thousands of scholars and built research universities ranked among India's private leaders; Nadar has given away several billion dollars, largely to education.
